inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Titan follows a well-defined gold hedging policy aiming to remain fully hedged at all times. Gold is sourced via three channels: gold metal loans (GML) from banks, customer exchange (old gold), and spot market purchases. For gold metal loans, quantity is fixed at procurement while liability/pricing is fixed at utilisation (typically aligned with customer sales), creating a natural hedge. For spot purchases, Titan hedges exposure by entering into future/forward contracts on commodity exchanges based on anticipated sales. This is a commodity (gold price) hedging policy rather than a disclosed USD-revenue hedging policy; no explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage or standalone forex/USD payables hedging quantum was found in available sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company disclosures (via CARE Ratings/ICRA credit rating reports and Titan filings referencing bullion hedge accounting) describe Titan as remaining fully hedged on gold procurement through gold metal loans, customer exchange, and commodity futures/forward contracts; since gold is an internationally USD-priced commodity, this creates indirect INR/USD linkage, but the AR MD&A/Notes text itself could not be directly read (PDF fetch blocked by 403) to confirm a standalone USD hedging policy or export revenue %. Titan's international jewellery footprint (Tanishq + Mia) reached 23 stores including UAE (Dubai, Sharjah, Abu Dhabi), Qatar, Singapore, and new FY25 stores in USA (Atlanta, Santa Clara); Q4FY25 international jewellery business grew ~69% YoY to ₹402 crore, but no disclosed % of total consolidated revenue was found.
